Figure 2:Denoising consistency and context redundancy.(a)At an intermediate denoising statet=t′t=t^{\prime}, a local step-to-final
extrapolation (red dashed) can deviate from the final denoised
state without context (A→BA\!\to\!B). Relevant context concentrates the
conditional outcome, aligning the extrapolation more closely with the final
state (C→DC\!\to\!D). Our policy treats content that is consistently predictable
from existing context as redundant, pruning low-discrepancy tokens while
retaining high-discrepancy tokens.(b)Curves report the
MSE between thex0x_{0}prediction at each intermediate denoising step and the
finalx0x_{0}. The Causal Forcing, LongLive, and Self-Forcing plots compare runs
with and without the available context KV: first-frame KV for Causal Forcing
and Self-Forcing, and preceding-chunk KV for LongLive. For LingBot World v2,
which does not support text-to-video generation, both runs use an initial frame
and rotate the camera: “with context” means that the content revealed after
rotation appeared earlier in the context, whereas “without context” means
that it did not. In all four comparisons, the with-context condition has lower
error across the plotted steps, consistent with our criterion.
